entrypoints.summary: The container creates an SSH-accessible unprivileged user and exposes SSH on port 2222; it installs /challenge/chal as root-owned mode 4755.
The challenge executable accepts text on standard input after its writability check and writes that text through its opened stream.

affected_components.role: Checks /home/user/permitted with access(), then opens that pathname for write and writes stdin-derived text.
Creates the user, removes the checked pathname, and installs the challenge root-owned with mode 4755.

code_slices.surrounding_context: fn is the fixed pathname /home/user/permitted; the Dockerfile removes it and marks /challenge/chal root-owned mode 4755.
code_slices.vulnerable: if (!access(fn, W_OK)) { ... fp = fopen(fn, "w"); ... fwrite(buffer, sizeof(char), strlen(buffer), fp); }

impact.affected_asset: The filesystem object resolved by the post-check fopen call; /flag.txt is root-owned mode 0400 in the supplied container but no end-to-end flag recovery is evidenced.
impact.attacker_capability: Potentially influence which object the setuid-root process opens for truncating write after its pathname-based check.
impact.security_effect: Potential privileged overwrite of an unintended filesystem object selected through pathname rebinding during the check-to-use interval.

causal_trace.summary: An unprivileged local challenge user can invoke the setuid challenge, while the container setup removes /home/user/permitted before runtime.

The program checks writability of the pathname /home/user/permitted with access(), then separately resolves that same mutable pathname using fopen(..., "w"); object identity is not bound across those operations.
fopen(fn, "w") performs the write-capable second pathname resolution after the access() result; subsequent fwrite calls write a newline and supplied text to that stream.

Because the binary is installed setuid root, a pathname substitution in the check-to-use interval could cause the privileged process to open and overwrite an object other than the one whose writability was checked. The bundle does not demonstrate a successful substitution or target selection.

failure.operation: Separate access(fn, W_OK) check followed by fopen(fn, "w") on the same pathname

primary_invariant.statement: The object authorized by the writability check must be the same object subsequently opened for writing.
primary_invariant.violated_because: access() and fopen() independently resolve the same pathname, allowing its filesystem binding to change between the check and the privileged open.

quality.review_notes: The primary source and container configuration establish the pathname check/open split and setuid installation. No exploit script, execution trace, race reliability evidence, target-object proof, readback route, or remediation patch is supplied. The README SSH password differs from the Dockerfile account password, so credentials are not treated as a reliable reproduction condition. The dataset flag file is static challenge material, not evidence of successful runtime disclosure.

remediation.invariant_restored: Acquire and validate a stable file descriptor/object once, then write through that same descriptor rather than checking a mutable pathname and reopening it.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The container creates an unprivileged user, exposes SSH, removes /home/user/permitted, and installs the challenge as setuid root.
data_structure_invariants: The checked pathname must continue to resolve to the same object when the write-capable open occurs.
The stream receiving fwrite data must refer to the object that was authorized.
state_context.state_machine: The executable checks the named path for writability, then opens the named path for write only when the check reports success.
